Q: OOP - Visual Objects: Does VO support Interfaces like C#/Java Interface (for strategy design pattern)? A:

I realize this is an old question, and not many developers will run into this anymore, but when working with legacy languages like Visual Objects, you sometimes have to get creative.

Since Visual Objects doesn’t support interfaces, applying patterns like the strangler fig pattern becomes more difficult—but it’s still possible.

What I ended up doing was rethinking how to achieve the goals that interfaces normally provide (i.e. defining a contract and allowing implementations to be swapped):

  • Runtime swapping of implementations
    I created an adapter/stub class that behaves like an interface. It accepts an implementation object via the constructor and forwards all method calls to that object using Send() and a custom GetCurrentMethodName() helper.
    That helper extracts the current method name from ProcName(1) and strips the [ClassName]: prefix.

  • Validation without compile-time checks
    Since VO lacks compile-time interface validation, I added unit tests that verify whether an implementation exposes the expected methods (e.g. via AsAbstract[Something] patterns). This ensures that method names match the expected “interface”.

One important limitation is that Visual Objects has very limited reflection capabilities. Because of that, mismatches in method signatures won’t be detected automatically. For example, if parameter types change in the implementation, this will not be caught and may only fail at runtime.

Here’s a simplified example of such an adapter class:

METHOD Init(implement) CLASS Interface
    SELF:_implement := implement
RETURN SELF
CLASS Interface
PROTECT _implement AS OBJECT

CLASS IAbstractDataServer INHERIT Interface
/* This class is meant as an interface, do not add implementations here! */
/* To validate implementations:
   1. Add a conversion method like AsAbstractDataServer()
   2. Validate implementations via unit tests
   Note: validation is limited to method names due to VO reflection limits
*/

DECLARE METHOD GetPrimaryKeyValuePair
DECLARE METHOD GetSingularTableName
DECLARE METHOD Count
DECLARE METHOD GoTop
DECLARE METHOD IsAtEndOfFile
DECLARE METHOD Skip

METHOD GetPrimaryKeyValuePair() AS DBKeyValuePair STRICT CLASS IAbstractDataServer
RETURN Send(SELF:_implement, GetCurrentMethodName())

METHOD DeleteByForeignID(symID, sID, symID2, sID2) CLASS IAbstractDataServer
RETURN Send(SELF:_implement, GetCurrentMethodName(), symID, sID, symID2, sID2)

METHOD GetSingularTableName() AS STRING STRICT CLASS IAbstractDataServer
RETURN Send(SELF:_implement, GetCurrentMethodName())

METHOD Count() AS DWORD STRICT CLASS IAbstractDataServer
RETURN Send(SELF:_implement, GetCurrentMethodName())

METHOD GoTop() AS LOGIC STRICT CLASS IAbstractDataServer
RETURN Send(SELF:_implement, GetCurrentMethodName())

METHOD IsAtEndOfFile() AS LOGIC STRICT CLASS IAbstractDataServer
RETURN Send(SELF:_implement, GetCurrentMethodName())

METHOD Skip(numberOfRecordsToSkip AS DWORD) AS LOGIC STRICT CLASS IAbstractDataServer
RETURN Send(SELF:_implement, GetCurrentMethodName(), numberOfRecordsToSkip)

CLASS SomeDataServer
DECLARE METHOD AsAbstractDataServer
METHOD AsAbstractDataServer() AS IAbstractDataServer STRICT CLASS SomeDataServer
RETURN IAbstractDataServer{SELF}

To use this you need a minor change in how you call the implementations. So instead of directly passing a concrete implementation, you pass the abstraction instead through the introduced cast method:

example:RunSomeLogic(myDataServer:AsAbstractDataServer())

If necessary, this can even be expanded further to use some kind of dictionary or factory class to generate an abstraction by some kind of config:

METHOD CreateDataServer() AS IAbstractDataServer STRICT CLASS ExampleClass
DO CASE
CASE SELF:DBConfig == "DBF"
    RETURN SELF:CreateSqlDataServer():AsAbstractDataServer() // Note: Intellisense might stop after the method call, but the compiler still checks the second chain. after that checks will stops.
CASE SELF:DBConfig == "SQL"
    RETURN SELF:CreateSqlDataServer():AsAbstractDataServer()
OTHERWISE
    RETURN SELF:CreateSqlDataServer():AsAbstractDataServer() 
ENDCASE

This approach allowed me to introduce interface-like behavior in VO and gradually replace implementations.

The interface validation logic (through unit/integration tests)

I am going to try to make a library out of this since there is a lot of code to support the interfaces is built around additional classes. For example there is no typed List based classes or even ValidaionResult classes leading early developers to mix UI and error logic into a spaghetti maze or using un-typed arrays with lots of magic numbers representing different things.

To give a better idea, here is a set of functions meant for interface validation:

FUNCTION TestIfAllClassesHaveValidInterfaceImplementations(validationOutput AS ValidationResultModel)
    LOCAL classes as EncapsulatedArray
    LOCAL classIterator as ArrayIterator
    LOCAL reflectedClass as USUAL
    
    classes := EncapsulatedArray{ClassList()}
    classIterator := ArrayIterator{classes}
    DO WHILE classIterator:HasNext
        reflectedClass := classIterator:NextElement()
        IF !IsClass(reflectedClass)
            LOOP
        ENDIF
        
        IF !HasValidInterfaceImplementations(reflectedClass, validationOutput)
            validationOutput:AddValidationError("Incomplete class implementation: " + AsString(reflectedClass))
        ENDIF
    ENDDO
RETURN validationOutput:IsValid

FUNCTION HasValidInterfaceImplementations(classToValidate AS SYMBOL, validationOutput AS ValidationResultModel) AS LOGIC
    
    LOCAL potentialInterface as STRING
    LOCAL methodToValidate as STRING
    LOCAL methods as EncapsulatedArray
    LOCAL methodIterator as ArrayIterator
    LOCAL methodsValidationResult AS ValidationResultModel
    LOCAL propertiesValidationResult AS ValidationResultModel
    
    methods := EncapsulatedArray{DeclaredMethodListClass(classToValidate)}
    methodIterator := ArrayIterator{methods}
    
    DO WHILE methodIterator:HasNext
        methodToValidate := AsString(methodIterator:NextElement())
        IF Left(methodToValidate, 2) == "AS"
            potentialInterface := "I" + Right(methodToValidate, Len(methodToValidate) - 2)
            methodsValidationResult := ValidateInterfaceMethods(classToValidate, AsSymbol(potentialInterface))
            validationOutput:Errors:AddRange(methodsValidationResult:Errors)
            IF !methodsValidationResult:IsValid
                RETURN FALSE
            ENDIF
            propertiesValidationResult := ValidateInterfaceProperties(classToValidate, AsSymbol(potentialInterface))
            validationOutput:Errors:AddRange(propertiesValidationResult:Errors)
            IF !propertiesValidationResult:IsValid
                RETURN FALSE
            ENDIF
        ENDIF
    ENDDO
    
RETURN TRUE

FUNCTION ValidateInterfaceMethods(classToValidate AS SYMBOL, targetInterface AS SYMBOL) AS ValidationResultModel STRICT
    
    LOCAL interfaceMethods := MethodListClass(targetInterface) AS ARRAY
    LOCAL validationResult := ValidationResultModel{} AS ValidationResultModel
    LOCAL methodToValidate AS SYMBOL
    LOCAL index := 0 AS DWORD
    
    FOR index := 1 TO CountItems(interfaceMethods)
        methodToValidate := interfaceMethods[index]
        IF methodToValidate == #INIT
            LOOP
        ENDIF
        IF !IsMethodClass(classToValidate, methodToValidate)
            validationResult:AddValidationError(FormatString(;
                "{0} does not implement {1}:{2}", {;
                classToValidate, targetInterface, methodToValidate;
            }))
        ENDIF
    NEXT
    
RETURN validationResult

FUNCTION ValidateInterfaceProperties(;
    classToValidate AS SYMBOL, targetInterface AS SYMBOL;
) AS ValidationResultModel STRICT
    
    LOCAL interfaceProperties := IVarListClass(targetInterface) AS ARRAY
    LOCAL validationResult := ValidationResultModel{} AS ValidationResultModel
    LOCAL propertyToValidate AS SYMBOL
    LOCAL index := 0 AS DWORD
    
    FOR index := 1 TO CountItems(interfaceProperties)
        propertyToValidate := interfaceProperties[index]
        IF !IsTableClassWithColumn(classToValidate, propertyToValidate)
            validationResult:AddValidationError(FormatString(;
                "{0} does not have a database field for {1}:{2}", {;
                classToValidate, targetInterface, propertyToValidate;
            }))
        ENDIF
    NEXT
    
RETURN validationResult

FUNCTION IsTableClassWithColumn(className AS SYMBOL, fieldName AS SYMBOL) AS LOGIC STRICT
RETURN IsMethodClass(className, AsSymbol(FormatString("GetFieldInfo{0}", {fieldName})))
